text: The ability to generate new questions offers a way for AI systems to expand the challenges available for evaluation and learning. For visual questions, however, a generated question–answer pair can have a correct answer according to the generation process while that answer is not recoverable from the image itself. This makes automatic verification difficult, because checking the information used during generation does not establish that the answer is actually supported by the image. Using vision–language models to perform this check introduces a different problem: validity then depends on the capabilities of the models being evaluated. We introduce DualLoop, a system in which coding agents propose visual questions and write two programs: one generates question instances and expected answers, while the other solves them from images alone. We study whether the system can keep expanding the question collection, whether agents can control which parts of an image matter for the answer, and whether model errors can guide generation. The collection continues to grow across question types, agents usually follow the image-region requests, and frontier-model feedback produces questions that are much harder for open-weight models. Fine-tuning on generated examples improves held-out performance, including an average +2.2-point gain across 16 external benchmarks.
